title: Incremental JavaScript-to-TypeScript Migration
subtitle: Convert a real plain-JS feature set to fully typed TypeScript, incrementally, without a rewrite
description: Take an existing plain-JavaScript task-management feature -- API layer, utility functions, and React components -- and migrate it to TypeScript file by file, the way a real team would on a live codebase.
overview: You'll be given a working plain-JS feature (a task list with API calls, formatting utilities, and components). Rather than rewriting it from scratch, you'll convert it incrementally: model the underlying data first, then type the functions that touch it, then the components, coexisting with any remaining JS files via allowJs. You'll practice modeling nullable vs. optional fields, typing fetch responses honestly, using discriminated unions for request state, and avoiding any as a shortcut.

milestones.title: Milestone 1: Model the Data Layer
milestones.description: Define shared interfaces for the API's actual response shapes, distinguishing nullable from optional fields.

tasks.title: Define a Task interface from real sample API responses
tasks.description: Model id, title, dueDate (nullable), and completed, based on actual response payloads rather than assumptions.
hints: A field the API always sends but sometimes as null needs `| null`, not `?`.

tasks.title: Model request state as a discriminated union
tasks.description: Define a RequestState<T> type with idle/loading/success/error variants sharing a status field.
hints: Switch on the shared status field to narrow safely in consuming code.

tasks.title: Type the fetchTasks function's return value
tasks.description: Wrap the return type in Promise<Task[]> and avoid asserting the response as any.
hints: res.json() is any by default -- type the parsed value as unknown and validate before trusting it.

milestones.title: Milestone 2: Type the Utility and Component Layer
milestones.description: Convert formatting utilities and React components to TypeScript without falling back to any anywhere.

tasks.title: Type formatDueDate and validateTaskText
tasks.description: Both functions currently accept untyped parameters; add explicit parameter and return types.
hints: formatDueDate needs to accept string | null to match the Task interface.

tasks.title: Convert TaskCard.jsx to TaskCard.tsx
tasks.description: Define a TaskCardProps interface for task and an onComplete callback, typed as (id: number) => void.
hints: Import the shared Task interface rather than redefining the shape locally.

tasks.title: Convert TaskList.jsx to TaskList.tsx, consuming RequestState<Task[]>
tasks.description: Switch on the request state's status field to render loading, error, and success UI distinctly.
hints: This is where the discriminated union from Milestone 1 pays off.

milestones.title: Milestone 3: Verify the Migration Holds Under Change
milestones.description: Prove the migration actually catches real mistakes, and document your incremental strategy.

tasks.title: Introduce and then fix a deliberate type mismatch
tasks.description: Temporarily pass a number where Task.title expects a string, confirm TypeScript catches it, then fix it.
hints: This is your evidence the migration adds real safety, not just satisfies the compiler cosmetically.

tasks.title: Add a new deleteTask(id: number): Promise<void> function fully typed from scratch
tasks.description: No JS starting point this time -- write it directly in TypeScript.
hints: This tests whether you can type new code, not just convert existing code.

tasks.title: Write a short migration strategy writeup
tasks.description: Document the order you converted files in and why, as if explaining the approach to a team lead.
hints: Justify starting with shared types before components.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Zero any usage
acceptanceCriteria.description: No file in the migrated feature uses any anywhere in its type annotations.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Correct nullable vs. optional modeling
acceptanceCriteria.description: Fields that are always present but sometimes null use `| null`; fields that may be entirely absent use `?`.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Request state modeled as a discriminated union
acceptanceCriteria.description: Loading, error, and success UI states are driven by switching on a shared status field, not separate boolean flags.

acceptanceCriteria.title: New code written TypeScript-first
acceptanceCriteria.description: deleteTask is written directly in TypeScript with no JS starting point, fully typed.

resources.description: Official guidance on allowJs/checkJs and incremental migration strategy.

title: Test Suite and Security Hardening Sprint
subtitle: Take an under-tested, vulnerable feature to production-ready: layered tests plus a real security audit
description: Given a small existing 'user profile' feature with no tests and two planted security issues, build a layered test suite and run a full security audit, fixing what you find.

milestones.title: Milestone 1: Layered Test Suite
milestones.description: Build unit, component, and integration test coverage for the profile feature.

tasks.title: Unit-test the extracted bio-length validation logic
tasks.description: Cover valid input, empty input, and over-length input with Vitest.
hints: Arrange-act-assert keeps each case readable.

tasks.title: Component-test the ProfileForm's loading/error/success states
tasks.description: Use React Testing Library queries by role/label, not CSS class.
hints: Don't skip the error and empty states -- they're the most commonly missed.

tasks.title: Integration-test the save flow against a mocked API with MSW
tasks.description: Mock only the network boundary; let real component and validation logic run.
hints: Cover both a successful save and a server-side validation error response.

tasks.title: Document your test coverage decisions
tasks.description: Write a short note explaining what you tested at each layer and why.
hints: Frame it as you would in a pull request description.

milestones.title: Milestone 2: Security Audit
milestones.description: Apply a real security checklist to the feature and find the two planted vulnerabilities.

tasks.title: Run the XSS/CSRF/CORS/token-storage checklist against the feature
tasks.description: The bio field renders user content, and the auth token is stored somewhere -- check both carefully.
hints: One vulnerability is in how content renders; the other is in where the token lives.

tasks.title: Fix the unsanitized bio rendering with DOMPurify
tasks.description: The profile bio currently uses dangerouslySetInnerHTML with no sanitization.
hints: Preserve legitimate formatting while stripping executable content.

tasks.title: Move the auth token from localStorage to an httpOnly cookie
tasks.description: Update both the login flow and how subsequent requests authenticate.
hints: Remember this reopens a CSRF consideration -- add SameSite as part of the fix.

milestones.title: Milestone 3: Prioritized Findings Report
milestones.description: Write the audit up the way a real security review would be delivered to a team.

tasks.title: Write a findings report ranking issues by real exploitability
tasks.description: Explain why the XSS-plus-localStorage-token combination is a chained, critical finding.
hints: A finding without a specific fix isn't a complete audit.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Three-layer test coverage
acceptanceCriteria.description: The feature has unit, component, and integration test coverage, not just one layer.

acceptanceCriteria.title: No unsanitized HTML rendering
acceptanceCriteria.description: All user-generated content rendered as HTML is sanitized with a maintained library.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Token not readable by JavaScript
acceptanceCriteria.description: The auth token is stored in an httpOnly cookie, not localStorage or sessionStorage.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Findings report includes specific fixes
acceptanceCriteria.description: Every finding in the report specifies an exact remediation, not just a flagged concern.

title: Client-Rendered App to Next.js App Router Migration

tasks.title: Recreate the catalog's routes using file-based routing

tasks.title: Convert the product detail page to fetch data directly in an async Server Component

milestones.title: Milestone 2: Server/Client Boundary and Mutations
milestones.description: Draw the Server/Client Component boundary correctly and move the add-to-cart flow to a Server Action.

tasks.title: Implement addToCart as a Server Action

tasks.title: Configure environment variables correctly for deployment

tasks.title: Deploy to a live, publicly accessible URL

tasks.title: Measure and record Core Web Vitals before and after the migration

acceptanceCriteria.description: Each route's rendering strategy (static/ISR/dynamic) is chosen deliberately and documented with a reason.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Server Action validates and authorizes
acceptanceCriteria.description: addToCart validates input and checks authentication server-side, not relying on client-side checks alone.

title: Accessible Component Library Audit & Remediation
subtitle: Take an existing, visually-complete component library from inaccessible to WCAG-conformant
description: You're given a small component library (modal, dropdown menu, tabs, form inputs) that looks correct but was built with zero accessibility consideration. Audit it against a real checklist and remediate every component.
overview: Each component in the starter library has at least one real accessibility gap: the modal doesn't trap or restore focus, the dropdown is unreachable by keyboard, the tabs have no ARIA roles, and a form input relies on a placeholder instead of a real label. You'll run both automated and required manual (keyboard-only and screen-reader) audits, then fix each component while preserving its existing visual design and API.

milestones.title: Milestone 1: Audit
milestones.description: Run the full accessibility checklist against every component, combining automated tooling with required manual verification.

tasks.title: Run an automated scan (axe or Lighthouse) against each component
tasks.description: Record every finding, even ones you already suspect are false positives.
hints: Automated tools catch under half of real issues -- don't treat this as the complete audit.

tasks.title: Complete a full keyboard-only pass through every component
tasks.description: Unplug your mouse and try to operate the modal, dropdown, tabs, and form using only Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, and arrow keys.
hints: Note every place focus gets lost, skipped, or has no visible indicator.

tasks.title: Complete a full screen-reader pass through every component
tasks.description: Use VoiceOver, NVDA, or a mobile screen reader to interact with each component and note what's announced incorrectly or not at all.
hints: Pay special attention to whether the modal announces itself when it opens.

milestones.title: Milestone 2: Remediate Each Component
milestones.description: Fix every finding from Milestone 1 without breaking the components' existing visual design or public API.

tasks.title: Fix the Modal: focus trap, focus restoration, and Escape to close
tasks.description: Focus should move into the modal on open and back to the trigger button on close.
hints: role="dialog" and aria-modal="true" are part of the fix, but focus management is the harder half.

tasks.title: Fix the Dropdown: full keyboard support and ARIA roles
tasks.description: Arrow keys to navigate options, Enter to select, Escape to close, with role="listbox"/"option".
hints: Check whether a native <select> could replace this entirely for simpler cases.

tasks.title: Fix the Tabs and the form input's missing label
tasks.description: Add proper tab/tablist/tabpanel roles and replace the placeholder-only input with a real associated label.
hints: A visually-hidden label is fine if the design can't accommodate a visible one.

milestones.title: Milestone 3: Re-Verify and Document
milestones.description: Confirm every fix actually resolves the original finding, and document the audit for the rest of the team.

tasks.title: Re-run the full keyboard and screen-reader pass against the fixed components
tasks.description: Confirm every originally-noted issue is actually resolved, not just visually plausible.
hints: Re-verification is not optional -- a fix that looks right isn't confirmed until you've actually tested it the same way you found the bug.

tasks.title: Write an audit report documenting each finding and its fix
tasks.description: Format it the way you'd hand it to a design systems team lead.
hints: Prioritize by real user impact, not by category count.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Full keyboard operability
acceptanceCriteria.description: Every component can be fully operated using only a keyboard, with a visible focus indicator throughout.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Focus management on the modal
acceptanceCriteria.description: Focus moves into the modal on open and back to the trigger on close, with no keyboard trap beyond the intended one.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Accurate accessible names throughout
acceptanceCriteria.description: Every control has a correct accessible name via native semantics, a real label, or aria-label -- not a placeholder alone.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Manual verification documented
acceptanceCriteria.description: The audit report includes findings from the required manual keyboard and screen-reader passes, not only automated tool output.

title: From Product Spec to Architecture Plan
subtitle: Turn a real, messy product requirements document into a concrete technical architecture and build plan
description: You're given an actual product spec for a 'team task board' feature -- written by a product manager, with ambiguities, undefined edge cases, and competing stakeholder asks. Turn it into a technical plan you could hand to a team.
overview: The spec describes what the feature should do from a user's perspective but leaves real technical decisions open: how state is structured, what's client vs. server-owned, how real-time updates should work, and what happens in edge cases the spec doesn't mention. You'll extract the actual requirements, identify the ambiguities worth clarifying versus the ones you can reasonably resolve yourself, and produce an architecture plan with justified tradeoffs.

milestones.title: Milestone 1: Extract and Question the Spec
milestones.description: Read the spec critically, separating clear requirements from ambiguous or missing ones.

tasks.title: List every explicit functional requirement in the spec
tasks.description: Extract concrete, unambiguous requirements as a checklist.
hints: Distinguish 'must have' language from 'nice to have' or aspirational language.

tasks.title: List every ambiguity or undefined edge case
tasks.description: What happens if two users edit the same card simultaneously? What happens offline? The spec doesn't say.
hints: A good technical read of a spec surfaces the questions a product manager didn't think to answer.

tasks.title: Decide which ambiguities you'll resolve yourself vs. flag for clarification
tasks.description: Not every open question needs a meeting -- some have a reasonable default a competent engineer can just decide.
hints: Justify each decision briefly rather than picking silently.

milestones.title: Milestone 2: Architecture Decisions
milestones.description: Make and justify the real technical decisions the spec leaves open.

tasks.title: Decide the state ownership model: what's client state vs. server-owned
tasks.description: Card position during a drag is a good example of a genuinely debatable boundary.
hints: Consider what needs to survive a page refresh versus what's purely transient UI state.

tasks.title: Decide how real-time updates between collaborators should work
tasks.description: Polling, websockets, or a simpler eventual-consistency approach -- justify the tradeoff.
hints: Consider the actual expected team size and update frequency, not a hypothetical worst case.

tasks.title: Choose a rendering strategy for the board's initial load
tasks.description: Should the board be server-rendered, client-rendered, or something in between?
hints: Tie this back to what you learned about SSR/SSG/ISR tradeoffs earlier in the course.

milestones.title: Milestone 3: Write the Plan
milestones.description: Produce a document a real engineering team could actually build from.

tasks.title: Write the architecture plan with explicit tradeoffs for each major decision
tasks.description: Each decision should state what you chose, what you didn't, and why.
hints: A plan that only states conclusions without tradeoffs is much less useful to a reviewing team.

tasks.title: Break the plan into a rough milestone sequence a team could execute
tasks.description: What would be built first, and why that order?
hints: Sequence by what unblocks the most subsequent work, not just by perceived difficulty.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Requirements and ambiguities separated clearly
acceptanceCriteria.description: The plan distinguishes explicit spec requirements from ambiguities the author identified and resolved.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Every major decision includes a stated tradeoff
acceptanceCriteria.description: State ownership, real-time strategy, and rendering strategy each include what was chosen, what was rejected, and why.

acceptanceCriteria.title: Plan is sequenced, not just listed
acceptanceCriteria.description: The plan proposes a build order with reasoning, not just a flat list of decisions.

resources.title: React — Thinking in React
resources.description: A useful model for breaking a spec down into a structured technical plan.

resources.title: web.dev — Rendering on the Web
resources.description: Reference for the rendering-strategy decision in Milestone 2.

portfolioTips.bullet: Translated an ambiguous product spec into a full technical architecture plan, including state ownership, real-time sync strategy, and rendering approach, with documented tradeoffs.
Walk through how you decided which spec ambiguities to resolve yourself versus flag for product clarification.
Discuss the tradeoff you made between real-time collaboration complexity and simpler eventual consistency.
